nri-world.title: India's Restaurant Empires Are Crossing Borders. The Target Is Not Expats — It Is Everyone.

nri-world.nri_angle: Indian cuisine abroad has long been shaped by diaspora-run independents — the corner curry houses, the family-owned dosa joints, the biryani spots that serve as cultural anchors for NRI communities. The new wave of branded Indian restaurant chains entering the US, UK, and Gulf markets represents a shift from community comfort food to global mainstream ambition, powered by diaspora demand but no longer limited to it.

nri-world.title: A 17-Year-Old in Ontario Found the Flaw That Medical Science Missed for 53 Years. The Fix Fits in a Formula.
nri-world.excerpt: Gurnoor Kaur's EigenPulse corrects a mathematical error in pulse oximeters that has been misreading oxygen levels in darker-skinned patients since the 1970s. She is 17.
nri-world.image_caption: A pulse oximeter measuring blood oxygen levels on a patient's finger
nri-world.nri_angle: A Punjab-origin student in Canada solved a medical device flaw that disproportionately harms patients with darker skin — a problem the global medical establishment had accepted as intractable for decades. Her story illustrates how diaspora youth, straddling multiple worlds, bring perspectives that established institutions miss.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A State Senator, a Biotech Pioneer, and a Banker Who Came From Mumbai. Connecticut Just Honoured Five Indian Americans Who Built Careers Across Continents.
nri-world.excerpt: GOPIO-Connecticut's 20th anniversary gala on June 13 will recognise achievers in politics, antiviral research, journalism, banking, and engineering — each of them a case study in what the diaspora looks like when it puts down roots.
nri-world.image_caption: Connecticut State Senator Sujata Gadkar-Wilcox, one of five Indian Americans being honoured at GOPIO-CT's 20th anniversary gala
nri-world.nri_angle: Each of the five honourees represents a different facet of the Indian American experience in New England: a Fulbright scholar who became a state senator, a biotech founder whose antiviral technology is in clinical trials in Africa, a journalist who also practices clinical social work at Yale, a banker who rose from Mumbai University to lead a 174-year-old community bank, and an IIT Kharagpur graduate with 10 US patents. Together, they illustrate how deeply the diaspora has woven itself into Connecticut's institutional fabric.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Sent 112 Companies to Canada in Its Largest-Ever Trade Delegation. The Diaspora Built the Landing Strip.

The 1.9 million Indo-Canadians who made it all possible were sitting in the front row.
nri-world.image_caption: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who led India's largest-ever business delegation to Canada
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indo-Canadian diaspora — 1.9 million strong and growing — served as the connective tissue for the largest Indian business delegation ever sent abroad. The visit explicitly credited the community with bringing the two nations closer through business engagement and people-to-people ties, while CEPA negotiations that could reshape NRI trade corridors inch toward a year-end deadline.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Just Doubled the Equity Limit for Every NRI Investor. The Real Target Is the $40 Billion Gap.

nri-world.image_caption: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra at a press conference in Mumbai
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs who invest in Indian equities through the Portfolio Investment Scheme just had their individual caps doubled. For the first time, any overseas Indian — not just NRIs and OCIs — can buy listed Indian shares through PIS. This changes the calculus for every diaspora investor with an Indian brokerage account.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Four Players of Indian Origin Will Take the Pitch at the FIFA World Cup. India Still Won't Be There.

nri-world.nri_angle: The India-USA Trade Facilitation Portal positions diaspora professionals as the connective tissue in bilateral commerce, offering MSMEs, women-led businesses, and ODOP artisans a bridge to American markets that previously required expensive intermediaries.

nri-world.nri_angle: Drāvida represents a new wave of diaspora dining that refuses to flatten South Asian food into a single 'Indian' category — it celebrates the culinary traditions born when Indians moved to the Caribbean, East Africa, Southeast Asia and beyond, giving second-generation diners a menu that mirrors their own layered identities.

nri-world.title: India's Trade Deal With Oman Just Went Live. For 700,000 Gulf Indians, It's More Than Tariffs.

technology.title: India's UPI Just Went Live in Cambodia. Ten Countries and Counting.
technology.excerpt: NPCI's QR-based payment system now covers 4.5 million Cambodian merchants, part of a methodical push to build a global remittance-killing payments layer.
technology.image_caption: Close-up of a contactless payment using a smartphone and QR code
technology.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion could eventually disrupt the remittance industry that moves $137.7 billion annually to India. For NRIs sending money home through Wise, Western Union, or bank wires, UPI corridors operating at near-zero cost represent a direct alternative. The Cambodia launch is the latest signal that India's payment rails are going global.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Indian Immigrants Built 96 US Unicorns. None Cracked the Top Five.
technology.excerpt: A new NFAP study finds India leads the world in producing billion-dollar startup founders — but the biggest prizes still elude them.
technology.image_caption: Entrepreneur presenting a startup pitch to investors
technology.nri_angle: Indian immigrants have founded 96 US unicorns worth $5 trillion, making India the world's top source of billion-dollar startup founders. IIT Delhi (16 founders) and IIT Bombay (14) are the pipeline. But amid tightening immigration policy and H-1B uncertainty, the infrastructure that enabled this is under threat.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TCS, Infosys, and Wipro Just Deployed AI to 300,000 Workers. Their Stock Crashed Anyway.
technology.excerpt: India's IT giants completed one of the world's largest enterprise AI rollouts in six months. Investors responded by wiping 6% off the Nifty IT index in a single session.
technology.image_caption: Aerial view of the Glass Pyramid at the Infosys campus in Mysuru, India
technology.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs have family members working at TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, or hold stock in these companies. The AI disruption paradox — adopt AI or get replaced by it — is deeply personal for the diaspora, especially as Indian IT services firms are the largest H-1B sponsors in the US.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Apple Gave Up on Building Its Own AI Brain. Sundar Pichai and Jensen Huang Won the Contract.
technology.excerpt: The new Siri will run on Google's Gemini models powered by NVIDIA's Blackwell chips — a rare capitulation from the most vertically integrated company on earth.
technology.image_caption: Jensen Huang presenting NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture at CES 2025 in Las Vegas
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEOs Sundar Pichai (Google) and Jensen Huang's NVIDIA are the invisible engine behind Apple's biggest AI bet. For the thousands of Indian engineers at all three companies, this partnership reshapes internal power dynamics and career trajectories.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Joins the Trillion-Dollar Club. Three Visa Rejections Couldn't Stop Him.
technology.excerpt: The Kanpur-born, BITS Pilani-educated CEO now leads one of America's ten most valuable companies. Three of the world's priciest tech firms are run by Indians who arrived with engineering degrees and middle-class resolve.
technology.image_caption: Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of Micron Technology, now leads one of America's ten most valuable companies
technology.nri_angle: Mehrotra completes an extraordinary Indian-origin trifecta atop trillion-dollar tech: alongside Satya Nadella at Microsoft and Sundar Pichai at Alphabet. Micron is also building a $2.75 billion ATMP facility in Gujarat — a direct bet on India's semiconductor future.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Jensen Huang Called Marvell the 'Next Trillion-Dollar Company.' Its Biggest Lab Is in India.
technology.excerpt: NVIDIA's CEO anointed the networking chipmaker at Computex, sending its stock up 30%. What Wall Street may not know: Marvell's largest R&D centre outside California sits across four Indian cities.
technology.image_caption: Server racks in a modern data center, the kind of infrastructure Marvell's networking chips connect
technology.nri_angle: Marvell employs over 1,000 engineers in Bangalore alone, with additional design centres in Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai — making it a major employer of Indian semiconductor talent and a key beneficiary of India's chip design ecosystem.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google Just Cut the Cybersecurity Team It Paid $5.4 Billion For. AI Got the Budget Instead.
technology.excerpt: Sundar Pichai raised $85 billion last week for AI infrastructure. Days later, Google quietly laid off staff from Mandiant and its Threat Intelligence Group — the elite units that track state-sponsored hackers.
technology.image_caption: Computer code on a dark screen, representing the cybersecurity work now being restructured at Google
technology.nri_angle: Google Cloud employs thousands of Indian engineers, many on H-1B visas. Cybersecurity teams at Google, including Mandiant, have significant Indian representation — and these workers face the 60-day grace period clock if their roles are eliminated.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Indian Tech Workers Built Dallas's Hottest Suburb. Now They're Leaving and Prices Are Cratering.
technology.excerpt: Home prices in Collin County fell 9% as H-1B crackdowns, AI-driven layoffs, and a $100,000 visa fee gut the buyer pipeline that made North Texas boom.
technology.image_caption: Aerial view of a suburban neighbourhood in the United States
technology.nri_angle: Indian H-1B workers drove 70% of luxury home sales in North Dallas suburbs. The collision of 123,000 tech layoffs, a $100,000 H-1B fee, and FHA mortgage bans for non-permanent residents is forcing families to sell at losses or consider returning to India.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX IPO Wants $75 Billion From You. Indian Engineers Built Half the Rockets.
technology.excerpt: The largest public offering in history lists next week at a $1.75 trillion valuation. NRI investors face a rare retail window — and an extraordinary price tag.
technology.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 first stage lands at Landing Zone 1 in Cape Canaveral
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers form a significant part of SpaceX's workforce, and NRI investors with Fidelity, Schwab, or Robinhood accounts can participate in the 30% retail allocation — a rare chance to buy into a company that normally only lets insiders in.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Cybersecurity Startup Innefu Labs Just Raised $30 Million. Its Client Is the State.
technology.excerpt: The 15-year-old Delhi company builds AI for India's intelligence agencies and defence apparatus. A Singapore-backed Series B now puts it on the path to an IPO.
technology.image_caption: Server infrastructure in a secure data centre facility
technology.nri_angle: Indian defence-tech is emerging as a real career path for NRI engineers at US contractors like Palantir and Raytheon. Innefu's IPO trajectory signals India's growing sovereign AI ambitions and offers NRI investors exposure to a sector that didn't exist five years ago.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks Just Hit $3 Billion in a Quarter. The Stock Still Fell.
technology.excerpt: The IIT Varanasi grad has turned a firewall company into a $250 billion cybersecurity platform. Wall Street's response to his best quarter yet was to take profits.
technology.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, at TechCrunch Disrupt
technology.nri_angle: Nikesh Arora's journey from IIT Varanasi to running the world's most valuable cybersecurity company is an instructive arc for Indian-American tech professionals. His platformisation bet mirrors the integration-over-fragmentation instinct that many Indian engineering leaders bring to enterprise tech.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Diljit Dosanjh Premiered the Trailer of His Partition Film at a Packed Toronto Stadium. Advance Bookings Have Opened in North America First.
entertainment.excerpt: Imtiaz Ali's Main Vaapas Aaunga reunites Diljit with A.R. Rahman after Chamkila, tells a love story across 1947 and the present, and is releasing in North American theatres a week before India. The diaspora is the audience.
entertainment.image_caption: Diljit Dosanjh performing during his AURA Tour
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Bobby Deol Just Delivered the Performance of His Career. The Film Got 500 Screens. It Might Not Need More.
entertainment.excerpt: Anurag Kashyap's Bandar premiered at TIFF, earned four-star reviews, and opened to rave word-of-mouth. But in a week dominated by Peddi and franchise sequels, it is fighting for every screen it can get.
entertainment.image_caption: Bobby Deol at a film event
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.image_caption: Shilpa Shinde at a public event in Mumbai

entertainment.title: Made In India: A Titan Story Is Now Streaming for Free. It May Be the Best Indian Series of 2026 So Far.
entertainment.excerpt: Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah turn the origin of India's biggest watch brand into six hours of riveting television. The NRI nostalgia runs deep.
entertainment.image_caption: Jim Sarbh, who plays Xerxes Desai in Made In India: A Titan Story
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Welcome To The Jungle Has 24 Stars, a June 26 Date, and Akshay Kumar's Best Comic Instincts. Bollywood Is Betting Big on Nostalgia.
entertainment.excerpt: The third Welcome film arrives with the biggest ensemble cast in recent Hindi cinema history and a distribution deal that covers theatres, TV, and streaming in one sweep.
entertainment.image_caption: Akshay Kumar, who leads the 24-member cast of Welcome To The Jungle
entertainment.nri_angle: The Welcome franchise has always been disproportionately popular with overseas Indian audiences, becoming a staple of NRI family movie nights. The June 26 release targets the summer window when diaspora families are most likely to visit theatres together.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Five Indian Actors Are Building Real Hollywood Careers. Not Cameos. Careers.
entertainment.excerpt: From Alien: Earth to The Knife, Adarsh Gourav, Ali Fazal, Ishaan Khatter, Riccha Sinha, and Disha Patani are no longer crossing over. They are staying.
entertainment.image_caption: Adarsh Gourav, who plays a lead role in Ridley Scott's Alien: Earth series
entertainment.nri_angle: For Indian Americans who grew up watching Bollywood while consuming Hollywood, these actors represent the first generation to build genuine dual-industry careers — changing what stories get told and what characters get written.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Avantika Vandanapu Has Been Named Harvard's South Asian Person of the Year. She Is 19.
entertainment.excerpt: The Telugu-American Mean Girls actress is being celebrated for breaking barriers in Hollywood — even as a rumoured Tangled casting sparks a debate about which roles South Asians are allowed to play.
entertainment.image_caption: Avantika Vandanapu, Indian-American actress and Harvard's South Asian Person of the Year
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: South Asian Filmmakers Are Building Their Own Pipeline from Cannes to Tribeca. Here Is How.
entertainment.excerpt: Box Office Guru Media's initiative connects diaspora creatives with studios, agencies, and distributors through structured pitch sessions and industry networking.
entertainment.image_caption: The Cannes Film Festival, where South Asian filmmakers gathered for networking and pitch events
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ninety Minutes of Weight Training a Week Lowers Your Risk of Dying by 13 Per Cent. The Study Tracked 147,000 People for 30 Years.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The largest-ever study on strength training and longevity found a sweet spot of 90 to 120 minutes a week — with the biggest surprise being a 27 per cent drop in neurological disease deaths.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person performing dumbbell strength training exercises at a gym
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A British-Made Pill Just Shrank Tumours Across Six Cancer Types. Every Patient Had Run Out of Options.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Oxford-developed drug GRWD5769 strips away cancer's 'invisibility cloak,' allowing immunotherapy to work in patients where it had failed. The ASCO results are early but remarkable.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Cancer researchers at a clinical trial laboratory studying immunotherapy treatments
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The First Major Trial of Probiotics for Cancer Treatment Just Began. The Science Behind It Is Rooted in Your Gut.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Nearly 700 patients will test whether a common Japanese probiotic can boost immunotherapy. South Asians, whose traditional diets are rich in fermented foods, have reason to watch closely.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A scientist examines bacterial cultures in a research laboratory
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Three Obesity Drugs Just Stole the Show at ADA 2026. South Asians Should Pay Close Attention.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Roche's injection hit 22.7 per cent weight loss in 48 weeks. An oral pill showed no liver damage. A third drug barely caused nausea. The obesity treatment landscape is about to change.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A researcher works in a pharmaceutical laboratory developing new drug treatments
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs May Cut Cancer Risk by Up to 70 Per Cent. Five ASCO Studies Explain Why South Asians Should Pay Attention.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Pancreatic, lung, breast and blood cancers all showed significant reductions among GLP-1 users in studies covering nearly 900,000 patients presented this week
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A GLP-1 receptor agonist injection pen used for weight management and diabetes treatment
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The AHA Just Said Exercise Works Even When the Scale Does Not Move. South Asians Need to Hear This.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new scientific statement in Circulation documents that physical activity improves blood pressure, insulin resistance and visceral fat independently of weight loss
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Regular physical activity improves cardiovascular health even without significant weight loss
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India’s Heatwave Has Killed 56 People and Caused 25,000 Cases of Suspected Heatstroke Since March. If You Are Visiting This Summer, Read This.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Thirty-four people died in a single district in Uttar Pradesh in two days — all over 60 with preexisting conditions. Temperatures have breached 42 degrees Celsius across northern India while power outages leave families without fans or running water.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Scorching temperatures across India have caused 25,000 suspected heatstroke cases since March
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The diaspora summer travel season — June through August, aligned with American and British school holidays — coincides directly with India’s most dangerous heat period. NRIs travelling with elderly parents or young children face specific medical risks.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Unsafe Food Kills 1.5 Million People a Year. South-East Asia and Africa Bear Three Quarters of the Burden.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A WHO report covering 194 countries finds that chemical contamination from arsenic and lead now causes 73 per cent of foodborne deaths, children under five face triple the risk, and the global productivity cost exceeds 300 billion dollars annually. The diaspora implications are personal.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Street food vendors prepare meals — unsafe food causes 866 million illnesses a year globally
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs travelling to India face direct exposure to foodborne risks that disproportionately affect South-East Asia, while families importing traditional foods should be aware of arsenic in rice and lead contamination in spices.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One in Three World Cup Matches Faces Dangerous Heat. FIFA Just Banned Fans From Bringing Water Bottles.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: With the tournament kicking off on June 11 across 16 North American cities, an NPR analysis finds 39 matches at high risk for heat illness — and diaspora fans attending in Houston, Dallas, and Miami face the worst conditions.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fans watch a soccer match under sunny skies at an outdoor stadium
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Swapping 100 Grams of Conventional Produce for Organic Each Day Cuts Breast Cancer Risk by 10 Per Cent. The Data Is Getting Hard to Ignore.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A seven-year French study of 31,000 women finds that even modest shifts toward organic fruits and vegetables significantly reduce postmenopausal breast cancer risk — with implications for South Asian families navigating pesticide-heavy food systems on two continents.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh vegetables and fruits displayed at a local market
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One in Seven People Now Uses an AI Chatbot Instead of Seeing a Doctor. The Risks Are Not What You Expect.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A major UK study finds 15 per cent of the public has replaced GP visits with AI, while a separate trial shows chatbots matching physicians on diagnosis. For a diaspora facing three-month specialist waits, the implications are personal.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fifteen per cent of the British public has used AI chatbots instead of contacting a GP for health concerns
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Sleeping Less Than Six Hours a Night Raises Your Osteoarthritis Risk by Up to 40 Per Cent. Night-Shift Workers Face Even Worse Odds.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A half-million-person WashU study links short sleep and disrupted circadian rhythms to accelerated joint damage, with implications for every South Asian working late shifts abroad.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Participants who slept fewer than six hours a night showed significantly higher risk of joint disease in the UK Biobank study
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
